newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary needs to stem social sec. deficit - minister.
newsitem.headline: Hungary needs to stem social sec. deficit - minister.

text.p: Hungary's finance minister Peter Medgyessy said on Monday that, without new measures to cancel out the country's spiralling, social security deficit the gap could reach 80 billion forints next year.
"If the government did nothing with the social security system, the deficit would grow to 80 billion forints (in 1997)," Medgyessy told the Hungarian International Press Association on Monday.
The Finance Ministry expects Hungary's social security deficit to run as high as 53 billion forints ($335.4 million) this year, compared with a target of 17.8 billion forints.

In order to stem the tide the government has included in its 1997 draft budget plans to introduce across-the-board social security contributions that no longer exclude the low paid and which would result in a zero balance in the social security budget.
"The social security contribution rules will be unfavourable for those companies which pay low wages," Medgyessy said. "But the 80 billion forint gap must be filled.
The key 1997 budget figures are likely to be approved by Parliament by the end of November and the budget law, which the House began to discuss last week, is expected to be passed around Christmas.
